subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should browser private-network SSRF handling gain core confirmation, allow/block, or temporary-grant semantics, and which first-stage policy shape is approved?
rationale: The request changes browser egress security semantics and public config/CLI surface; source inspection shows no existing approval or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Staged Policy First
options.body: Define explicit allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata behavior, docs, and tests before considering interactive prompts.

options.title: Approve Interactive Confirmation Now
options.body: Commit to user approval UX with timeout, rate limiting, session scoping, and audit behavior across browser navigation paths.

options.title: Keep Current Strict Model
options.body: Continue with strict default plus host exceptions and document broad private-network access as a trusted-environment opt-in only.

recommendation.title: Approve Staged Policy First
recommendation.body: Define explicit allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata behavior, docs, and tests before considering interactive prompts.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest current-source and recent merged-history signal across browser SSRF config, navigation, CDP policy, and shared SSRF helpers.
